A layer-by-layer look at OpenMind’s hardware-agnostic architecture, its Natural Language Data Bus, and what it takes to run a language model on a real machine.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Inside OM1: The Robot Runtime That Turns Sensor Data Into SentencesOM1 is an open-source runtime that sits between a robot’s hardware and a large language model. This article walks through how it is built, one layer at a time: how raw sensor data becomes text, how that text is merged into a single prompt, how the model’s response turns back into motion, and how the whole system is described in a configuration file you can edit.
Along the way, I cover the runtime, the middleware options, the observability stack, and the parts of the design that need care before you put them in production.
By the end, you will know what each component does, why the pieces fit together the way they do, and how to run the stack on your own machine.
Reference here.
The Problem OM1 Is Built Around
Most robotics middleware moves numbers. Point clouds, quaternions, twist messages, joint states. OM1 moves sentences. That one decision shapes everything above and below it in the stack, and it is the reason the project is worth studying even if you never buy a robot.
